description: Prepares owner review for a new BotSpot deployment; this call does not start a bot or place trades before approval. After explicit owner approval, this is HIGH RISK: the deployment may place real-money trades. Call for an authorized start request even when required saved variables are missing: readiness validation returns the exact missing-variable secure entry cards. Preparing those cards is the next setup step, not a completed start or approval. Never request secret values in chat or claim a schedule was created by this preparation. For an extra iteration of an existing scheduled bot, use run_deployment_once; do not create another deployment. Never use this tool for a direct or one-off buy, sell, or order request. Use place_trade instead; a start_deployment approval is not a trade approval. When the user asks to run, start, turn on, or deploy an attached saved strategy, call this tool to create the website approval request; do not substitute a backtest. Omit brokerCredentialId by default unless the user explicitly named the exact saved broker connection/account to use now. The website approval page is the normal place for visible broker selection and blocks approval until a valid broker is selected. This tool accepts only saved references: aiStrategyRevisionId for code, optional brokerCredentialId for broker access, and optional envVarSetIds for saved non-broker runtime secrets. Broker access must come from a saved broker credential selected in the tool call or on the website approval page. deploymentMode defaults to auto. Auto lets BotSpot choose always-on or scheduled from schedule metadata or schedule policy; the resolved route is shown on the approval action and locked for execution. Use deploymentMode='always_on' only when the user explicitly asks to run continuously. Use deploymentMode='scheduled' only when the user explicitly asks for a schedule and you can provide or reuse schedule metadata/policy. Explicit modes fail instead of silently changing route. When the user asks for a daily schedule and does not name a clock time, do not ask what time or timezone. Call this tool in the same turn with deploymentMode scheduled, runImmediately false, and scheduleMetadata schemaVersion 1, marketSession regular, liveCadenceMatchesBacktest true, source user_instruction, and cadence specific_times at 09:35 America/New_York (five minutes after the US market open, avoiding the turbulent opening minute). For a NEW deployment with an immediate first iteration (including afternoon intraday runs), set runImmediately=true. For one iteration of an EXISTING scheduled deployment, use run_deployment_once; never substitute this start operation or an update. Do not refuse by citing opening-range or market-open+N timing from the recurring schedule; that timing is trading eligibility for later ticks, not a ban on starting an owner-requested one-shot now. For a one-off clock time such as 3:10 p.m., prefer scheduleMetadata with specific_times or event_window for that time and runImmediately=true. For a one-time run "in N minutes", use an event_window window with startAfterApprovalMinutes (at least 3) and durationMinutes instead of startAt, so the run starts N minutes after the owner approves however long the approval takes. An exact startAt that is less than about 4 minutes away is refused, and its approval request expires before that time. Do not pass a broker credential whose status is reconnect_required. Omit brokerCredentialId and still create the start approval; the website approval page lets the owner select, add, or reconnect a broker before approving, including through /account-settings/broker-connections. Non-broker runtime secrets must come from saved environment variables: pass their ids as envVarSetIds. Do not pass raw broker credentials, raw environment variables, raw runtime configuration, inline code, requirements text, API keys, screener exports, CSV rows, JSON row dumps, workbook data, or large base64 blobs. Use broker_connections(action="connect_existing")/list_broker_credentials before deployment, and use saved_env_vars(action="create")/saved_env_vars(action="list") for data-provider API keys or other non-broker runtime secrets. Broker credential key examples: Kalshi (kalshi): KALSHI_API_KEY_ID + KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY. Optional: KALSHI_SUBACCOUNT, KALSHI_EXCHANGE_INDEX, KALSHI_BASE_URL, KALSHI_WS_URL. Do not pass KALSHI_IS_DEMO; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"KALSHI_API_KEY_ID":"key-id...","KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY":"private-key-pem..."}. Alpaca (alpaca): ALPACA_API_KEY + ALPACA_API_SECRET OR ALPACA_OAUTH_TOKEN. Do not pass ALPACA_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"ALPACA_API_KEY":"PK...","ALPACA_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Tradier (tradier): TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_ACCESS_TOKEN OR TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_API_KEY OR TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_TOKEN. Optional: TRADIER_REFRESH_TOKEN, TRADIER_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, TRADIER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET. Do not pass TRADIER_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER":"6AB12345","TRADIER_ACCESS_TOKEN":"token..."}. Charles Schwab (schwab): SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + SCHWAB_TOKEN. Example credentialValues: {"SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_NUMBER":"123456789","SCHWAB_TOKEN":"base64url-token-payload..."}. Tradovate (tradovate): TRADOVATE_USERNAME + TRADOVATE_DEDICATED_PASSWORD + TRADOVATE_CID + TRADOVATE_SECRET. Optional: TRADOVATE_APP_ID, TRADOVATE_APP_VERSION. Do not pass TRADOVATE_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"TRADOVATE_USERNAME":"username...","TRADOVATE_DEDICATED_PASSWORD":"dedicated-password...","TRADOVATE_CID":"client-id...","TRADOVATE_SECRET":"secret..."}. TopstepX (projectx-topstepx): PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_API_KEY + PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_USERNAME. Optional: PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_PREFERRED_ACCOUNT_NAME. Example credentialValues: {"PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_API_KEY":"key...","PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_USERNAME":"username..."}. WEEX (weex): WEEX_API_KEY + WEEX_API_SECRET + WEEX_API_PASSPHRASE. Example credentialValues: {"WEEX_API_KEY":"key...","WEEX_API_SECRET":"secret...","WEEX_API_PASSPHRASE":"passphrase..."}. Bitunix (bitunix): BITUNIX_API_KEY + BITUNIX_API_SECRET. Optional: BITUNIX_TRADING_MODE. Example credentialValues: {"BITUNIX_API_KEY":"key...","BITUNIX_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Kraken (kraken): KRAKEN_API_KEY + KRAKEN_API_SECRET. Example credentialValues: {"KRAKEN_API_KEY":"key...","KRAKEN_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Coinbase (coinbase): COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME + COINBASE_PRIVATE_KEY. Optional: COINBASE_API_PASSPHRASE, COINBASE_SANDBOX. Example credentialValues: {"COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME":"organizations/.../apiKeys/...","COINBASE_PRIVATE_KEY":"-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----..."}. Any other CCXT 4.5.64 exchange id (for example okx, binance, bybit, bitget, hyperliquid): use that id as the broker and the credentials it requires, named <EXCHANGE>_API_KEY, <EXCHANGE>_API_SECRET, <EXCHANGE>_API_PASSPHRASE, <EXCHANGE>_UID, <EXCHANGE>_PRIVATE_KEY or <EXCHANGE>_WALLET_ADDRESS. Do not pass <EXCHANGE>_SANDBOX; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. memoryGb may be 2, 3, or 4 when the user sets bot memory, including because the strategy needs a browser. Omit memoryGb to keep the current size. Do not send any other size, and do not send a CPU field. CPU stays as it is. Pass memoryGb only with deploymentMode scheduled. A 2, 3, or 4 GB always-on start is rejected because that larger host is not approved; tell the user that start was not placed instead of dropping the memory setting. The tool always creates a short-lived website authorization request and returns an approval URL the user must open while signed in to BotSpot. It does not execute from chat-only approval or reusable grants. No broker secrets are returned to the MCP response. For Codex, Claude, Cursor, and other clients without BotSpot native confirmation cards, return the exact authorizationUrl as a clickable Markdown link in your reply. Do not say a card or button was created unless the client actually rendered it. BotSpot clients may render structuredContent as a native confirmation, but a button name alone is not an approval link. A pending request is not execution; only the signed-in user may approve on the website. Report expiry and check get_deployment_action_status after approval.
